new_findings_not_in_handover.finding: The macrolide class row has zero erythromycin evidence. Its only evidence record is the clarithromycin label. If clarithromycin is moved to an exact child (SIM_B), the class row is left asserting a major warfarin interaction for erythromycin with no supporting evidence record at all.
new_findings_not_in_handover.required_action: Either source and review independent erythromycin evidence, or reduce/retire the class row rather than leaving an unevidenced single-member class.

new_findings_not_in_handover.finding: RxNorm exposes TWO distinct 500 mg oral-tablet concepts for clarithromycin: 'clarithromycin 500 MG Oral Tablet' and '24 HR clarithromycin 500 MG Extended Release Oral Tablet'. The PMBJP catalogue row for code 380 carries form_raw:null and only the brand string 'Clarithromycin Tablets IP 500 mg', which does not distinguish immediate-release from extended-release.
new_findings_not_in_handover.required_action: Code 380 cannot be bound to an exact presentation concept without disambiguating evidence. Excluded from this round. Precedent for handling an explicit ER concept separately exists (tramadol 24 HR ER, rxcui 833709).

new_findings_not_in_handover.finding: PMBJP drug code 380 (500 mg) does not appear anywhere in tender RC-222/2025, and no 500 mg clarithromycin line exists in that document. Only the 250 mg product is tendered there.
new_findings_not_in_handover.required_action: Code 380 has no official PMBI tender binding from the document set examined. A different official tender/amendment must be located and reviewed before code 380 may be proposed.

new_findings_not_in_handover.discovered_during: execution of approved items A1/A2 (attempting to record the product-presentation mapping)
new_findings_not_in_handover.finding: PMBJP drug codes carried in the catalogue snapshot do not reliably agree with the official PMBJP product list. Across every code shared between the catalogue (dist/latest/drugs.jsonl, janaushadhi rows) and the official product list PDF, only 568 of 1466 agree — a 38.7% agreement rate. The mismatch has a shifting-offset signature (catalogue code 51 carries the product the official list assigns to 48; catalogue 53 carries official 51; catalogue 55 carries official 52), consistent with either a row-alignment defect in the janaushadhi PDF parser or a different list edition with reassigned codes. The catalogue build provenance does not record which list edition or URL it was built from, so the two cannot be reconciled from the repository alone.
new_findings_not_in_handover.affects_codes_under_audit: Catalogue says 740 = clarithromycin 250 mg; the official list says 739 = clarithromycin 250 mg and 740 = Cefpodoxime Proxetil Dispersible Tablets 50 mg. Catalogue says 380 = clarithromycin 500 mg; the official list says 383, and code 380 is absent from the official list entirely.
new_findings_not_in_handover.affects_already_approved_mappings: Of the 17 already-approved product-presentation codes, 4 agree with the official list (1502 amiodarone 100 mg, 202 metronidazole 400 mg, 18 azithromycin 250 mg, 28 tramadol 50 mg), 7 disagree (430 -> official Nebivolol 5 mg; 2142 -> official Verapamil 40 mg; 400 -> official Cefixime+Clavulanate; 2034 -> official Potassium/Magnesium Citrate; 521 -> official Alfacalcidol; 2772 -> official Vincristine Injection; 1246 -> unresolved official row), and 6 codes are absent from the official list (2141, 452, 2771, 2773, 201, 72).
new_findings_not_in_handover.runtime_risk_assessment: LOW at runtime, HIGH for the evidence chain. Mapping resolution keys on product_id (a content hash of the catalogue product row) and revalidates product_assertion_sha256, returning status 'stale' on drift (src/lib/interaction-mapping.mjs). The PMBJP code is descriptive metadata in mapping_id and in the tender evidence identifier, NOT the resolution key, so a wrong code does not cause a runtime mis-resolution onto a different drug. However the human review evidence cites 'pmbjp-tender:RC-<n>/<year>:<code>:page-<n>', so a wrong code means the clinician approved against a citation pointing at the wrong tender row. The evidence chain, not the runtime binding, is what is compromised.
new_findings_not_in_handover.required_action: Do not record any further PMBJP product-presentation mapping until the code-identity question is resolved: establish which official list edition the catalogue snapshot was built from, record that provenance, and re-verify the already-approved codes' tender citations against it. Execution of approved items A1, A2 and A5 is halted pending this.

new_findings_not_in_handover.finding: A third clarithromycin-bearing PMBJP row exists that the handover did not list: code 2097, 'Combipack of Clarithromycin 500mg Tablets IP, Esomeprazole 40mg Tablets IP (Gastro resistant) and Tablets in Mono Amoxycillin 750mg Tablets IP Carton' (H. pylori eradication combipack). Its ingredient identity resolves to the separate canonical ingredient 'combipack of clarithromycin', not 'clarithromycin'.
new_findings_not_in_handover.required_action: Must be explicitly excluded. A combipack is not a single-ingredient oral tablet assertion and must never inherit a clarithromycin mapping.

openfda_clarithromycin_label.fragment_text: Spontaneous reports in the postmarketing period suggest that concomitant administration of clarithromycin and oral anticoagulants may potentiate the effects of the oral anticoagulants.

envelope_payload_sha256_drift.interpretation: The whole-response envelope hash differs because the openFDA API response envelope carries mutable meta (including last_updated). The content-bearing identifiers all match: set_id, spl_version 23, effective_time 20230530, and the verbatim fragment. This is envelope drift, not label content drift.

superseded_claim.why_retracted: The claim rested on a positional 1:1 alignment between the serial/drug-code column and the item-name column in a multi-column PDF table extraction. Cross-checking against the official PMBJP product list shows that alignment is unreliable: the official list assigns code 739 to 'Clarithromycin Tablets IP 250 mg' and code 740 to 'Cefpodoxime Proxetil Dispersible Tablets 50 mg'. The tender page-64 alignment reproduces the same off-by-one signature (it also yields 739 for Cefuroxime Axetil Tablets IP 125mg, which the official list assigns to 736, and 747 for Glimepiride 3mg, which the official list assigns to 746).
